definition: Abstain means to freely choose not to do something, especially through self-restraint.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abstain. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abstain should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: During training season the sprinter abstained from sugary drinks entirely.
Skip is casual and weaker — you might skip dessert once without a second thought; to abstain is to hold yourself back deliberately, usually as a sustained act of self-restraint.
Renounce is stronger than abstain: renouncing something means formally giving it up forever, not just choosing restraint for now.

Refrain means to stop yourself from doing a particular thing, usually briefly and in the moment - you refrain from interrupting. Abstain is self-denial with commitment behind it: freely giving up something you enjoy, often for a long stretch and for a reason like health or principle. You refrain from a remark; you abstain from caffeine for a month.

Forgo means to go without something, to give it up or do without - and it says nothing about why. You might forgo dessert simply because the line is too long. Abstain makes the reason part of the meaning: a free, deliberate act of self-restraint. Forgoing is the going-without; abstaining is the disciplined choice behind it.

Abstain means to freely choose not to do something, especially through self-restraint.
Every winter, Amir's family hosted a legendary dessert table: three pies, a chocolate fountain, his aunt's caramel bars.
This year Amir had promised his dentist a clean checkup after two rough visits.
He filled his plate with fruit, poured himself tea, and sat at the far end of the table.
When the caramel bars came around for the third time, he passed the tray along without taking one.
Choosing restraint when no one would have blamed him for indulging — that is what it means to abstain.
Amir freely passes up desserts he loves, out of deliberate self-restraint rather than outside pressure, which is exactly what abstaining is.
neutral-to-formal; health, ethics, and voting contexts
Abstain takes 'from' ('abstain from soda') and always implies a free choice — if allergies or rules stop you, you are not abstaining.
In parliamentary settings it has the special sense of declining to vote either way.

As student council president, Maya Chen ran the budget meetings but kept one iron rule for herself.
Whenever funding for the debate team came up — the club she had captained for two years — she handed the gavel to the vice president and abstained.
She cast no vote, argued no side, and let the count proceed without her, however much the outcome mattered to her friends.
Some members told her the rule was overcautious; nobody doubted her honesty.
Maya kept it anyway, all four semesters she served.
The one time the debate team's request lost by a single vote, she walked out with the losers and still did not say what she would have chosen.
